Find the faces of a segment graph

Source: R/faces.R
find_faces.Rd

Enumerate the faces of the graph formed by a pool's segments: the regions it encloses (street blocks between roads, parcels between boundaries), plus one outer face for each connected component.

Usage

find_faces(x)

Arguments

x

A wkpool (ideally after merge_coincident()).

Value

A data frame with one row per half-edge, in walk order face by face:

  • .face: face id, 1-based, in order of the lowest half-edge on it.

  • .vx0, .vx1: the half-edge's start and end vertex ids.

  • .segment: index of the input segment (in x) it comes from.

  • .adjacent: the face on the other side of the edge.

  • .face_area: signed area of the face (positive for bounded faces).

  • .bridge: TRUE when .adjacent is the same face.

Details

Segments are taken as undirected edges. A boundary carried by more than one feature (the same pair of vertex ids) counts once, keeping the first segment, and segments from a vertex to itself are dropped. Run merge_coincident() first so that segments meeting at the same coordinates share a vertex: faces are traced through shared vertex ids only, so lines that cross without a shared vertex (a bridge over a road) do not split each other, and their faces can overlap.

Each edge gives two half-edges, one per direction. At each vertex the outgoing half-edges are ordered counter-clockwise by angle, and a walk always takes the next edge clockwise from the one it arrived on, which keeps the face on its left. Every half-edge lies on exactly one face, so the result has two rows per edge. Bounded faces are counter-clockwise (positive area); the outer face of each connected component is clockwise (negative area), or zero for a component that encloses nothing (a tree).

An edge with the same face on both sides (.bridge) is a dead end, or a bridge joining two parts of the graph; its two half-edges both appear in that face's walk. Drop those rows to keep only edges that separate two faces.

Only x and y are used.

See also

find_neighbours() for adjacency between input features, find_cycles() for the rings of polygon input.

Examples

## a square with a cross inside: four blocks
x <- wk::as_wkb(c(
  "LINESTRING (0 0, 1 0, 2 0, 2 1, 2 2, 1 2, 0 2, 0 1, 0 0)",
  "LINESTRING (1 0, 1 1, 1 2)",
  "LINESTRING (0 1, 1 1, 2 1)"
))
pool <- merge_coincident(establish_topology(x))
f <- find_faces(pool)
## bounded faces and their areas
unique(f[f$.face_area > 0, c(".face", ".face_area")])
#>    .face .face_area
#> 1      1          1
#> 13     3          1
#> 17     4          1
#> 21     5          1
## which blocks share an edge
unique(f[f$.face_area > 0 & f$.face != f$.adjacent, c(".face", ".adjacent")])
#>    .face .adjacent
#> 1      1         2
#> 2      1         3
#> 3      1         5
#> 13     3         2
#> 15     3         4
#> 16     3         1
#> 17     4         2
#> 19     4         5
#> 20     4         3
#> 21     5         2
#> 23     5         1
#> 24     5         4
